D2-L02.intro: Describe relationships with family and friends — أَتَفَاهَمُ مَعَ، أَثِقُ بِـ، يَدْعَمُنِي، نَتَشَاجَرُ ثُمَّ نَتَصَالَحُ — and explain what makes a relationship strong, with reasons and examples.

roleplays.title: Who do you get on with?

tasks.task: Say who you get on with in your family.
tasks.en: I get on with my older sister.
Because she listens to me and helps me.

tasks.task: Say who you sometimes disagree with.
tasks.model: نَعَمْ، أَخْتَلِفُ مَعَ أَخِي الصَّغِيرِ أَحْيَانًا.
tasks.en: Yes, I sometimes disagree with my little brother.

tasks.task: ASK your classmate who they get on with most (they then answer).
tasks.en: And you, who do you get on with most?

tasks.model: صَدِيقِي المُقَرَّبُ اسْمُهُ عُمَرُ، وَنَقْضِي الوَقْتَ مَعًا بَعْدَ المَدْرَسَةِ.
tasks.en: My close friend is called Omar, and we spend time together after school.

roleplays.setting: Helping a friend after an argument
roleplays.title: Making up
roleplays.examiner: your friend, who argued with his brother

tasks.examiner: تَشَاجَرْتُ مَعَ أَخِي أَمْسِ. مَاذَا أَفْعَلُ؟
tasks.task: Give your friend two pieces of advice.
tasks.model: يَجِبُ أَنْ تَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَهُ بِهُدُوءٍ، وَأَنْ تَسْتَمِعَ إِلَيْهِ.
tasks.en: You should talk to him calmly and listen to him.

tasks.task: Say when you argue and what happens next.
tasks.model: أَحْيَانًا نَتَشَاجَرُ بِسَبَبِ التِّلْفَازِ، وَلٰكِنَّنَا نَتَصَالَحُ سَرِيعًا.
tasks.en: Sometimes we argue over the TV, but we make up quickly.

tasks.task: Describe how you made up last time (past).
tasks.model: آخِرَ مَرَّةٍ اعْتَذَرْتُ لِأُخْتِي، ثُمَّ شَاهَدْنَا فِيلْمًا مَعًا.
tasks.en: Last time I apologised to my sister, then we watched a film together.

tasks.examiner: … لِأَنَّهُ أَخَذَ هَاتِفِي مِنْ دُونِ إِذْنٍ.
tasks.task: ASK why they argued (your friend then answers).
Answer the unexpected question, with two reasons.
tasks.model: نَعَمْ، أَثِقُ بِهِمْ كَثِيرًا، لِأَنَّهُمْ يَدْعَمُونَنِي دَائِمًا وَيَحْفَظُونَ أَسْرَارِي.
tasks.en: Yes, I trust them a lot, because they always support me and keep my secrets.

tasks.examiner: مَنْ أَهَمُّ فِي حَيَاةِ الشَّابِّ: الأُسْرَةُ أَمِ الأَصْدِقَاءُ؟
tasks.model: فِي رَأْيِي الأُسْرَةُ أَهَمُّ، لِأَنَّهَا تَدْعَمُنَا دَائِمًا، وَلٰكِنَّ الأَصْدِقَاءَ يَفْهَمُونَ مُشْكِلَاتِ جِيلِنَا بِشَكْلٍ أَفْضَلَ.
tasks.en: In my opinion family matters more, because it always supports us, but friends understand our generation’s problems better.

tasks.task: Name three things and link them.
tasks.model: الثِّقَةُ وَالاِحْتِرَامُ وَالاِسْتِمَاعُ؛ فَعِنْدَمَا نَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى بَعْضِنَا نَتَفَاهَمُ، وَعِنْدَمَا نَتَفَاهَمُ تَصِيرُ العَلَاقَةُ أَقْوَى.
tasks.en: Trust, respect and listening; when we listen to each other we understand each other, and when we understand each other the relationship grows stronger.

tasks.examiner: حَدِّثْنَا عَنْ عَلَاقَةٍ تَغَيَّرَتْ فِي حَيَاتِكَ.
tasks.task: Describe a relationship that changed (past → present).
tasks.help: كُنْتُ … عِنْدَمَا كُنَّا … أَمَّا الآنَ فَـ … لِأَنَّنَا …
tasks.model: كُنْتُ أَتَشَاجَرُ مَعَ أَخِي كَثِيرًا عِنْدَمَا كُنَّا صَغِيرَيْنِ، أَمَّا الآنَ فَأَصْبَحْنَا صَدِيقَيْنِ، لِأَنَّنَا نَلْعَبُ فِي الفَرِيقِ نَفْسِهِ.
tasks.en: I used to argue a lot with my brother when we were small; now we have become friends, because we play in the same team.

tasks.examiner: … أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّهَا تُقَرِّبُ البَعِيدَ وَتُبْعِدُ القَرِيبَ.
tasks.task: ASK the chair’s opinion on social media and relationships (the chair then answers).
tasks.model: وَمَا رَأْيُكَ فِي تَأْثِيرِ وَسَائِلِ التَّوَاصُلِ عَلَى العَلَاقَاتِ؟
tasks.en: And what do you think of the effect of social media on relationships?

tasks.examiner: كَيْفَ سَتَكُونُ عَلَاقَتُكَ بِأُسْرَتِكَ عِنْدَمَا تَدْرُسُ فِي الجَامِعَةِ؟
tasks.model: سَأَتَّصِلُ بِأُسْرَتِي كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، وَسَأَزُورُهُمْ فِي العُطَلِ، لِأَنَّ المَسَافَةَ يَجِبُ أَلَّا تُضْعِفَ العَلَاقَةَ.
tasks.en: I will call my family every day and visit them in the holidays, because distance shouldn’t weaken the relationship.

conversation.qen: Who do you get on with?
conversation.en: I get on with my mother.
My father helps me with homework.

conversation.qen: Do you have a close friend?
conversation.model: نَعَمْ، عِنْدِي صَدِيقٌ مُقَرَّبٌ اسْمُهُ آدَمُ.
conversation.en: Yes, I have a close friend called Adam.

conversation.qen: What do you do with your friends?
conversation.model: نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ القَدَمِ وَنَقْضِي الوَقْتَ مَعًا.
conversation.en: We play football and spend time together.

conversation.qen: Describe your relationship with a close friend.
conversation.starter: عَلَاقَتِي بِـ … قَوِيَّةٌ؛ نَعْرِفُ بَعْضَنَا مُنْذُ … وَأَثِقُ بِهِ لِأَنَّهُ …
conversation.model: عَلَاقَتِي بِآدَمَ قَوِيَّةٌ؛ نَعْرِفُ بَعْضَنَا مُنْذُ خَمْسِ سَنَوَاتٍ، وَأَثِقُ بِهِ لِأَنَّهُ صَادِقٌ.
conversation.en: My relationship with Adam is strong; we have known each other for five years, and I trust him because he is honest.

conversation.model: أُخْتِي تَدْعَمُنِي؛ تُسَاعِدُنِي فِي الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ، وَتُشَجِّعُنِي قَبْلَ الاِمْتِحَانَاتِ.
conversation.en: My sister supports me; she helps me with maths and encourages me before exams.

conversation.q: مَتَى تَخْتَلِفُ مَعَ أَحَدٍ فِي أُسْرَتِكَ؟
conversation.qen: When do you disagree with someone in your family?
conversation.model: أَخْتَلِفُ مَعَ أَخِي عِنْدَمَا يَأْخُذُ أَشْيَائِي، وَلٰكِنَّنَا نَتَصَالَحُ بَعْدَ قَلِيلٍ.
conversation.en: I disagree with my brother when he takes my things, but we make up soon after.

conversation.qen: How did you meet your close friend?
conversation.model: تَعَرَّفْتُ عَلَيْهِ فِي أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ فِي المَدْرَسَةِ الاِبْتِدَائِيَّةِ؛ جَلَسْنَا مَعًا وَأَصْبَحْنَا صَدِيقَيْنِ.
conversation.en: I met him on the first day of primary school; we sat together and became friends.

conversation.qen: What is the most important thing in a friendship?
conversation.starter: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ … أَهَمُّ شَيْءٍ؛ فَإِذَا … يَصْعُبُ أَنْ …
conversation.model: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الصِّدْقَ أَهَمُّ شَيْءٍ؛ فَإِذَا كَذَبَ الصَّدِيقُ مَرَّةً، يَصْعُبُ أَنْ نَثِقَ بِهِ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى.
conversation.en: I think honesty is the most important thing; if a friend lies once, it is hard to trust him again.

conversation.q: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ نُسَامِحَ الأَصْدِقَاءَ دَائِمًا؟
conversation.qen: Should we always forgive our friends?
conversation.starter: لَيْسَ دَائِمًا؛ يَجِبُ أَنْ … وَلٰكِنْ إِذَا …
conversation.model: لَيْسَ دَائِمًا؛ يَجِبُ أَنْ نُسَامِحَ عَلَى الأَخْطَاءِ الصَّغِيرَةِ، وَلٰكِنْ إِذَا تَكَرَّرَ الخَطَأُ الكَبِيرُ، فَمِنْ حَقِّنَا أَنْ نَبْتَعِدَ.
conversation.en: Not always; we should forgive small mistakes, but if a serious mistake is repeated, we have the right to step away.

conversation.q: قَارِنْ بَيْنَ عَلَاقَتِكَ بِأَبِيكَ وَعَلَاقَتِكَ بِأُمِّكَ.
conversation.qen: Compare your relationship with your father and with your mother.
conversation.model: أَتَكَلَّمُ مَعَ أُمِّي عَنْ مَشَاعِرِي، بَيْنَمَا أَتَكَلَّمُ مَعَ أَبِي عَنِ الرِّيَاضَةِ وَالدِّرَاسَةِ؛ كِلَاهُمَا يَدْعَمُنِي بِطَرِيقَةٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ.
conversation.en: I talk to my mother about my feelings, whereas I talk to my father about sport and studies; both support me in a different way.

conversation.q: لَوْ تَشَاجَرْتَ مَعَ صَدِيقِكَ المُقَرَّبِ، كَيْفَ تَتَصَالَحَانِ؟
conversation.qen: If you argued with your close friend, how would you make up?
conversation.model: لَوْ تَشَاجَرْنَا، لَانْتَظَرْتُ حَتَّى نَهْدَأَ، ثُمَّ لَاعْتَذَرْتُ وَدَعَوْتُهُ إِلَى بَيْتِي لِكَيْ نَتَكَلَّمَ بِصَرَاحَةٍ.
conversation.en: If we argued, I would wait until we calmed down, then apologise and invite him round so we could talk openly.
